On 20/03/2024, 6:03 PM, "Zoë Bloom" <Zoe.Bloom@afpbloom.com> wrote:

 

Dear Nadia

 

I am sorry you remain so unwell. 

 

The current position is that my firm is owed around £12,000. I remind you that under the terms of the letter of instruction dated 24 January 2024 (attached), you agreed to liquidate your 401K and pay USD30,000 to my firm’s client account and provide a bank guarantee. You did not comply with those terms. If you had complied with the terms, I would have sufficient money both to discharge the outstanding fees and continue to act until the liquid sums had been used.

 

If we are reinstructed, then the fees will depend on what we are instructed to do. If it is simply to appear in court for the judgment then Brent will charge a refresher which I anticipate will be £8,000. My fees will be incurred on an hourly basis. Brent will then proceed to draft the court’s order but that will be a simple process of translating the judgment of the court into the court’s order.  It will not be a case of trying to renegotiate or relitigate what the Judge has decided. 

 

If I am reinstructed, and you ask me to instruct Brent then he will not charge you for carriage of the order (i.e. drafting it in liaison with the other side). That would be included within the brief fee. Obviously, if he has to go to court then he will charge for that (alongside any other consultations that you require). The difficulty for him, I envisage, is that because he does not act on a direct access basis, he would need to be instructed by me which would require you to instruct me. He could not just otherwise draft the order because he would be without instructions from you. I say this because I want to make clear that neither he nor I are attempting to charge you for something (i.e. the drafting of the order) which would otherwise have formed part of the brief fee on the basis of the original instruction. I hope this is clear.

 

To reiterate, the fees which would be incurred to attend a hearing where judgment is handed down to be in the region of £5,000 for me and £8,000 for Brent. There will also be my fees incurred on an hourly rate for any work I do with Brent and you on the order. This may be 6 hours work at around £3k. The total cost will be £16,000 on the basis that there is a hearing for the judgment. Less if there is not but at present we do not know how judgment will be handed down.

 

If the judgment is handed down in writing, and there is no hearing then any time will be incurred which does not relate to the simple drafting of the court’s order will be charged on an hourly basis by Brent and I. 

 

In any event, in order to resume my firm’s instruction the outstanding fees (c.£12k) will need to be discharged and I will require a payment on account of £16,000.

 

If you have any questions, please let me know.


Very best

Dear Zoe,

 

I am following up on the email exchange of yesterday.

 

As you are aware, I have been unwell for quite some time due to the abuse in the marriage and the respondent’s conduct during the proceedings.

 

The trial pushed my PTSD symptoms into unprecedented territories. At present I am suffering from a rapid heartbeat condition, gastric pain, and my left hand is numb. My nervous system has been utterly destroyed. I am starting EMDR sessions next week and I will attend an inpatient trauma programme as soon as I have my financial independence..

 

I am incapable of representing myself for the judgement and for drafting the orders under the current conditions.

 

Also, I am unable to speak with or communicate with the respondent for the rest of my life.

 

In emails dated 6 and 18 March, 2024 you made two following two statements: 

 

Statement 1 (email of 6 March 2024): “BRENT AND I WILL OBVIOUSLY COMPLY WITH OUR OBLIGATIONS TO THE COURT IN RELATION TO THE JUDGEMENT”.

 

Statement 2 (email of 18 March 2024): “We are currently off the record and don’t have instructions to come back on the record for the purposes of receipt of judgment and drafting the order. In the event that you find yourself in funds so that you can give us that instruction, we can discuss it then. “

 

Statements 1 and 2 are not consistent and I find this extremely confusing and distressing. 

 
Which one of these two statements is true, and which one is false? 
Is Brent representing me at the judgement?
Is Brent representing me for the drafting of the orders?
Are you representing me for the judgement?
Are you representing me for the drafting of the orders?
If any of the above answers is “No”, please could you send me an estimate of the fees required to represent me.
 

 

I need the above information as a matter of urgency in order to include in the LSPO application. 

 

I cannot represent myself for the judgment and the orders, and I have no funds. Therefore, the court must order the respondent to pay for my legal fees.

 

I will send the LSPO tomorrow if I don’t hear from you.

 

With kind wishes,

Nadia

On 20/03/2024, 6:03 PM, "Zoë Bloom" <Zoe.Bloom@afpbloom.com> wrote:

 

Dear Nadia

 

I am sorry you remain so unwell. 

 

The current position is that my firm is owed around £12,000. I remind you that under the terms of the letter of instruction dated 24 January 2024 (attached), you agreed to liquidate your 401K and pay USD30,000 to my firm’s client account and provide a bank guarantee. You did not comply with those terms. If you had complied with the terms, I would have sufficient money both to discharge the outstanding fees and continue to act until the liquid sums had been used.

 

If we are reinstructed, then the fees will depend on what we are instructed to do. If it is simply to appear in court for the judgment then Brent will charge a refresher which I anticipate will be £8,000. My fees will be incurred on an hourly basis. Brent will then proceed to draft the court’s order but that will be a simple process of translating the judgment of the court into the court’s order.  It will not be a case of trying to renegotiate or relitigate what the Judge has decided. 

 

If I am reinstructed, and you ask me to instruct Brent then he will not charge you for carriage of the order (i.e. drafting it in liaison with the other side). That would be included within the brief fee. Obviously, if he has to go to court then he will charge for that (alongside any other consultations that you require). The difficulty for him, I envisage, is that because he does not act on a direct access basis, he would need to be instructed by me which would require you to instruct me. He could not just otherwise draft the order because he would be without instructions from you. I say this because I want to make clear that neither he nor I are attempting to charge you for something (i.e. the drafting of the order) which would otherwise have formed part of the brief fee on the basis of the original instruction. I hope this is clear.

 

To reiterate, the fees which would be incurred to attend a hearing where judgment is handed down to be in the region of £5,000 for me and £8,000 for Brent. There will also be my fees incurred on an hourly rate for any work I do with Brent and you on the order. This may be 6 hours work at around £3k. The total cost will be £16,000 on the basis that there is a hearing for the judgment. Less if there is not but at present we do not know how judgment will be handed down.

 

If the judgment is handed down in writing, and there is no hearing then any time will be incurred which does not relate to the simple drafting of the court’s order will be charged on an hourly basis by Brent and I. 

 

In any event, in order to resume my firm’s instruction the outstanding fees (c.£12k) will need to be discharged and I will require a payment on account of £16,000.

 

If you have any questions, please let me know.


Very best

Dear Nadia

 

I cannot give you a binary answer, it is a little more nuanced than that as I have tried to explain. Please see the narrative explanation below (provided yesterday).

 

If we are reinstructed, then the fees will depend on what we are instructed to do. If it is simply to appear in court for the judgment then Brent will charge a refresher which I anticipate will be £8,000. My fees will be incurred on an hourly basis. Brent will then proceed to draft the court’s order but that will be a simple process of translating the judgment of the court into the court’s order.  It will not be a case of trying to renegotiate or relitigate what the Judge has decided. 

 

If I am reinstructed, and you ask me to instruct Brent then he will not charge you for carriage of the order (i.e. drafting it in liaison with the other side). That would be included within the brief fee. Obviously, if he has to go to court then he will charge for that (alongside any other consultations that you require). The difficulty for him, I envisage, is that because he does not act on a direct access basis, he would need to be instructed by me which would require you to instruct me. He could not just otherwise draft the order because he would be without instructions from you. I say this because I want to make clear that neither he nor I are attempting to charge you for something (i.e. the drafting of the order) which would otherwise have formed part of the brief fee on the basis of the original instruction. I hope this is clear.

 

To reiterate, the fees which would be incurred to attend a hearing where judgment is handed down to be in the region of £5,000 for me and £8,000 for Brent. There will also be my fees incurred on an hourly rate for any work I do with Brent and you on the order. This may be 6 hours work at around £3k. The total cost will be £16,000 on the basis that there is a hearing for the judgment. Less if there is not but at present we do not know how judgment will be handed down.

 

Very best

Dear Zoe,

On 16 January 2024 we attended a hearing at which my LSPO application was dismissed. M. MacDonald J. made an order to vary the Legal Service Provision made on 30 June 2023 at paragraph 8(b) “so that the payment of £151,000 shall be paid by 4pm on 17 January 2024 and shall be directed towards trial preparation and representation only”.  The order is attached to this email.

Weds 28.02.24 (8):     Judgment writing (no attendance required)

Thurs 29.02.24 (9):    Judgment writing (no attendance required)

Fri 01.03.24    (10)     (if not reserved) Judgment, order and costs.

 

My question is as follows: 

 

Are the legal costs for the entry “Judgement, order and costs” included in the payment of £151,000 in the attached court order?

 

I need a non-nuanced answer to the above question in order to write to the judge an informed and intelligent email regarding my legal representation.

Dear Nadia

 

I am really trying to communicate clearly and do want to help. I am concerned by the tone of your emails which is becoming increasingly aggressive and confrontational. This also happened when we last met in conference.  I am sure you do not mean to come across that way but if we are to continue to communicate I do ask you to be mindful of the way in which you engage with me. I am trying to help even if it does not seem that way.

 

The simple point is that I am not instructed and therefore Brent is not instructed. That is because you ran out of money to do the things you wanted to do. To the extent you want to reinstruct Brent to help you with the order then you will need a solicitor to instruct him. That doesn’t need to be me. 

 

In terms of the order, Brent’s brief included drafting it; nothing more. To undertake this task he needs a solicitor to be instructed - be it me or someone else. But the task is very limited – it is translating the judgment to an order, in the exact terms of the judgment. I am sorry if my language on 6 March caused any confusion. If reinstructed then Brent’s fee for translating the judgment to a simple court order is included in the brief but he will need a solicitor to assist. I have explained what I need if that solicitor is to be me. Another solicitor may be wiling to undertake the task for much less on account (and will not have arrears to be discharged) and indeed that may be best in light of our recent communication/tone etc. 

 

If you want anything else done by Brent, including reading emails, attending conferences or taking phone calls, then it will be new work and charged by him. No solicitor will be prepared to instruct him to do any of this work without funds on account to meet the costs.

 

If however, you only ask him to read the judgment and translate it into a court order then there is no additional counsel fee payable to you, only solicitor fees. It is up to individual firms to say what they need on account to assist you and I have explained what I will need if you wish to instruct me. If the money is not spent by you during the course of the instruction, it will be returned to you.

 

I hope this is clear. May I now update Detach?

 

Very best

Dear Nadia

 

I cannot give you a binary answer, it is a little more nuanced than that as I have tried to explain. Please see the narrative explanation below (provided yesterday).

 

If we are reinstructed, then the fees will depend on what we are instructed to do. If it is simply to appear in court for the judgment then Brent will charge a refresher which I anticipate will be £8,000. My fees will be incurred on an hourly basis. Brent will then proceed to draft the court’s order but that will be a simple process of translating the judgment of the court into the court’s order.  It will not be a case of trying to renegotiate or relitigate what the Judge has decided. 

 

If I am reinstructed, and you ask me to instruct Brent then he will not charge you for carriage of the order (i.e. drafting it in liaison with the other side). He could not just otherwise draft the order because he would be without instructions from you. I say this because I want to make clear that neither he nor I are attempting to charge you for something (i.e. the drafting of the order) which would otherwise have formed part of the brief fee on the basis of the original instruction. I hope this is clear.

 

To reiterate, the fees which would be incurred to attend a hearing where judgment is handed down to be in the region of £5,000 for me and £8,000 for Brent. There will also be my fees incurred on an hourly rate for any work I do with Brent and you on the order. This may be 6 hours work at around £3k. Dear Zoe,

 

I am sorry you find the tone of my emails “aggressive and confrontational”. I keep a running table of our emails which I attach to all my emails and which I invite you again to read in its entirety. 

 

I disagree with your qualification of the tone I use in my emails. I have maintained a professional and courteous tone throughout my emails as the attached correspondence demonstrates. 

 
Fact 1: Brent’s fee for the judgement and to draft the orders arising from the judgement are included in the original brief as per the judge’s order of 16 January 2024.
 
Fact 2: However, Brent cannot undertake this work (which is included in the original brief) unless he is instructed by you because he does not take Direct Access.
 
Fact 3: In order to be able to instruct Brent, you yourself must be instructed. 
 
Fact 4: You informed me on 18 March 2024 that your firm requires a minimum of £28,000 in order to be re-instructed (£12,000 to discharge the outstanding balance and £16,000 on account for the estimated work related to the judgement). 
 

Taken together, facts 1 to 4 create a chicken-and-egg situation where Brent cannot undertake work which is already included in his original brief unless I “find myself in funds”. 

 

This catch-22 is what I call a circular argument. We are back to the starting point and there is no progress.

 

This is not aggressive at all. This is a factual statement. We have a logic circularity.

 

We have a circularity problem which I must solve in order to secure my financial future and that of the children. 

 

I need proper assistance with the judgement and with the court orders. I need a legal team who will be extremely attuned to the potential danger post-divorce abuse represents in this case and a team who will work very hard to draft orders which will be air-tight and will protect the children and me from any potential future coercive control, manipulation, financial abuse, and cruelty. I need a legal team who will make sure there are no wink links in the court orders and no nooses around my neck when all is done.

 

I do not have any assets or liquidity under my name, and I cannot pay for these legal fees without the help of the court.

 

I have therefore emailed the judge to request his guidance.

 

In the meantime, I do not authorize you to write to Detach until I hear back from the judge. I informed him about the breach as well.

Nadia
